name: Lemony Spaghetti Carbonara with Prosciutto, Asparagus & Peas (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.

Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap). Add salt, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, uncover, add pasta, and stir for a few seconds; cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain pasta (reserving a ¼-cup pasta water before draining). Transfer 1 cup of pasta to a small bowl, and set aside. Return remaining pasta to the pot and cover to keep warm.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ tsp salt
8 oz spaghetti pasta

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ small bunch asparagus
½ lemon
¼ small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley
½ (16 oz) pkg strawberries

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, chop (or tear) prosciutto into bite-sized pieces.

Once the skillet is hot, add prosciutto and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy prosciutto to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Set aside a 1/4-cup for the kids' pasta, then place remaining Parmesan in a medium bowl.
Zest lemon into the medium bowl with the Parmesan. (Reserve lemon for later use)

Using a clean cutting board, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl, along with eggs, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine the Parmesan-egg mixture. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into 2-inch long pieces.

Return skillet to medium-high heat, add butter, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add asparagus, peas, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until asparagus is tender-crisp, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat and transfer 1 cup of asparagus and peas to a plate.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tsp butter, unsalted
1 cup frozen peas
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice strawberries. Add to the plate with the asparagus and peas.

Add the Parmesan-egg mixture to the pot with the cooked pasta, then toss continuously, until the pasta is glossy and evenly coated, about 1 minute. (The heat of the pasta will cook the egg.) Add reserved pasta water, 1 tablespoon at a time, if necessary, to loosen the pasta.
Juice reserved lemon into the pot, then add the crispy prosciutto, remaining asparagus, and peas. Toss once more to combine the spaghetti carbonara and set aside.
Cut the plain pasta into bite-sized pieces. Return to the bowl, along with butter and reserved Parmesan, then stir to combine the plain buttered pasta.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide plain buttered pasta, asparagus, peas, and strawberries between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide the spaghetti carbonara between plates or bowls and enjoy!
